title: Asymmetric Predictive Testing for Aging in SRAMs
problem: Current predictive testing methods for aging-induced SRAM failures use symmetric aggressive voltage conditions across read and write operations, resulting in significant over-testing that spuriously marks functional chips as defective.
motivation: Over-testing wastes yield; understanding asymmetric aging mechanisms can reduce false positives while maintaining coverage of genuinely at-risk SRAMs.
method: SRAM cells storing zeros experience asymmetric aging—they fail differently depending on whether you read them as zeros or ones. The method exploits this by testing each operation at a tailored voltage: writes at normal voltage, reads of zeros at aggressive voltage, and reads of ones at less-aggressive voltage. This replaces the uniform over-testing of standard approaches with targeted stress only where needed. Statistical sampling and simulation then quickly identify which chips actually fail.
key_novelty: Using different test voltages for each SRAM operation based on how it actually ages, rather than uniform aggressive conditions, reduces false rejections by 3-5× while still catching real failures.
contributions: Discovery of asymmetric aging in SRAMs causing read-1 failures in over-tested chips
Asymmetric predictive testing methodology with differential voltage application
3-5× reduction in over-testing for low under-testing limits
New statistical sampling and simulation method for accurate evaluation
limitations: Evaluation limited to SRAM aging; applicability to other memory technologies not discussed.
primary_theme: asymmetric aging-aware predictive testing for SRAM
